candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Treat mild hypoglycemia in an alert client who can swallow with 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate followed by glucose reassessment in 15 minutes.

options.B: Withhold oral intake until the next scheduled meal
options.C: Administer IV dextrose before attempting oral treatment
options.D: Give 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck glucose in 15 minutes

candidate.rationale: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 recommend treating hypoglycemia at 70 mg/dL or less with fast-acting carbohydrate in an alert person who can take oral carbohydrate. For most individuals, 15 g is used, with glucose rechecked 15 minutes later and treatment repeated if hypoglycemia persists.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Treat glucose ≤70 mg/dL with fast-acting carbohydrate; for most individuals give 15 g and recheck glucose after 15 minutes, repeating treatment if needed.
candidate.source_document_title: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.stem: An alert client with diabetes who can swallow has a blood glucose of 62 mg/dL and reports shakiness. What should the nurse do first?
